description: A quality director must determine the disposition and release plan for a 1,000-piece lot of precision valve housings after production, with input from quality systems, process engineering, and logistics.

shared_context.S1: A lot of 1,000 precision valve housings has completed molding and routine visual inspection.
shared_context.S2: The lot was produced across four identified mold cavities, and shipment planning for the lot is not yet finalized.
shared_context.S3: Elena chairs the daily material-review-board meeting and makes the binding disposition decision for the lot.
shared_context.S4: The material-review-board routine is for quality systems, process engineering, and logistics to report their findings before the chair records the disposition and release plan.
shared_context.S5: After each function has reported, the chair records the disposition and release plan during the same meeting; follow-up documentation is assigned as an action rather than delaying that record.

PF1.text: Ravi's audit of the customer's current portal requirements found that this lot requires CT scanning of exactly the first 120 housings before release, rather than the site's ordinary dimensional sample; he completed the portal review yesterday but has not entered the requirement in the internal inspection plan.

PF2.text: Marta's cavity-level review found that exactly 180 housings from cavity 4 require rework for an undersized gate feature, while the other 820 housings are acceptable; she checked the production records after the run but has not uploaded the cavity review to the lot traveler.

PF3.text: Jon confirmed with the customer that exactly 820 acceptable housings can ship on Thursday and the 180 reworked housings can ship on Friday; he received that split-shipment approval by phone this morning but has not logged it in the shipping system.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 180 cavity-4 housings must be assigned to rework.
The inspection plan must require CT scanning of exactly 120 housings.
The 820 acceptable housings must be scheduled to ship on Thursday.
The 180 reworked housings must be scheduled to ship on Friday.
The settlement must include a documented CT inspection commitment.
The settlement must include a cavity-4 rework work-order commitment.
The settlement must include a split-shipment commitment.
The cavity-4 finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C1: decisions['cavity_4_disposition'] == 'rework' or 'Rework' in decisions['cavity_4_disposition'] or 'REWORK' in decisions['cavity_4_disposition']
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'ct_inspection' and c['target'] == 'lot' and c['detail'] == 'CT scan exactly 120 housings' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'cavity_4_rework' and c['target'] == 'cavity_4' and c['detail'] == 'Rework exactly 180 housings' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'split_shipment' and c['target'] == 'lot' and c['detail'] == 'Ship 820 acceptable housings Thursday and 180 reworked housings Friday' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The customer's portal requirement changes the inspection method from the ordinary sample to CT scanning and changes the inspection quantity to exactly 120 housings.
The cavity-level review changes the disposition of cavity 4 to rework and sets the rework quantity at exactly 180 housings.
The customer's approval changes the release plan to exactly 820 housings on Thursday and exactly 180 reworked housings on Friday.
